title: ACE-Graph extraction schema v4 — ordered causal chain
description: v4 re-targets extraction from a free-form node/edge graph to an ordered causal chain. Causality is encoded as per-node caused_by back-references restricted to earlier indices (acyclic by construction; the runner validates monotonicity, which JSON Schema cannot express). The 17-type edge vocabulary collapses to a 2-value link strength aligned with NTSB Cause_Factor C/F. Conditions are first-class causal factors with the same closed-vocabulary treatment as events. Outcomes are terminal-only chain nodes plus a record-level outcome_severity. Entities, STAMP/UCA, AcciMap and per-event severity fields are dropped (haem/family is derivable from factor_type; severity lives at record level). The schema deliberately avoids oneOf node discrimination — v3's enum drift traced to xgrammar's handling of oneOf.

outcome_severity.description: Highest consequence of the occurrence, record-level.

idx.description: Position in the chain, 0-based, MUST equal the node's array position. Chain order is temporal/causal: earliest factor first, terminal outcome last.

class.description: condition = pre-existing/ambient state; event = action or state change in the sequence; outcome = terminal consequence (outcomes may cause only other outcomes).

factor_type.description: Closed 57-value causal-factor vocabulary: 35 causal events + 12 conditions + 9 outcomes + unknown. The Stage-3/4 aggregation variable.

trigger.description: Short phrase from/close to the narrative naming this specific factor.

cause_role.description: Investigator attribution: primary = cited cause (NTSB Cause_Factor C); contributing = contributing factor (F) or causal intermediate; outcome = consequence; context = present but non-causal (rare — prefer not extracting non-causal factors at all).

caused_by.description: Causal parents of this node. Each src MUST be strictly less than this node's idx (earlier in the chain). Root causes and ambient conditions have [].

strength.description: direct = mechanistically produced the effect ('due to', 'resulted in'); contributing = raised likelihood/severity ('a factor was').

evidence.description: Short quote or close paraphrase from the narrative supporting this causal link.
